title: Ambulatory transportation
heading: A little support. More independence.
summary: Transportation for passengers who walk independently or use a cane or walker.
detail: Share any walking aids, steps or boarding assistance needs when requesting a ride. The team can then confirm whether the vehicle and available support fit your trip.
question: Can I travel with a cane or walker?
answer: Tell the team which mobility aid you use and what assistance you need so they can confirm a suitable ride.
who: For passengers who can travel seated and walk independently or with a cane, walker or agreed assistance.
overview: Ambulatory describes the passenger’s mobility, rather than the reason for the appointment. Planning focuses on getting to the vehicle, boarding, storing walking aids and reaching the destination entrance. Tell us about the help you actually need so the team can check that the trip is suitable.
includes: A planned pickup and destination
Review of walking aids and boarding needs
Arrival timing and any return-trip request
prepare: Cane, walker or other walking aid
Steps, uneven paths and entrance access
Required arrival time and return plan

faqs.q: Is ambulatory transportation the same as wheelchair transportation?
faqs.a: No. Ambulatory transport is planned for someone who can walk and board with the agreed assistance. A passenger who needs to remain in a wheelchair requires a different vehicle arrangement.

faqs.q: Will someone help me inside the building?
faqs.a: Describe the assistance you need at both ends. Curbside, doorway and inside-building support are different arrangements; the team must confirm which help is available.

title: Wheelchair transportation
heading: Your mobility. Our attention.
summary: Accessible transportation arranged around your wheelchair and assistance needs.
detail: Include your wheelchair type, pickup access and any assistance requirements. The team must confirm vehicle compatibility and pickup arrangements before accepting the ride.
question: What details are needed for wheelchair transportation?
answer: Share your wheelchair type, pickup and destination addresses, appointment time and access conditions so the team can check suitability.
who: For passengers whose trip requires wheelchair access and a vehicle compatible with their chair and assistance needs.
overview: Wheelchair transportation planning covers more than vehicle space. The team needs to review the chair, boarding access and how the wheelchair and passenger will be secured. A power chair, scooter, wider chair or difficult entrance needs advance discussion; suitability is confirmed for the individual trip.
includes: Review of chair and vehicle compatibility
Access planning at pickup and destination
Boarding and securement arrangements
prepare: Manual chair, power chair or scooter type
Chair dimensions and combined weight if requested
Ramps, elevators, stairs and doorway access

faqs.q: Can I stay in my wheelchair during the ride?
faqs.a: Tell the team that you need to remain seated in your chair. They must confirm the vehicle, chair compatibility and appropriate securement before accepting the trip.

faqs.q: Can the driver carry a wheelchair up stairs?
faqs.a: Do not assume stair carrying or lifting is included. Describe every step and access barrier in advance so the team can review an appropriate arrangement.

title: Hospital discharges
heading: The next chapter starts at home.
summary: Transportation from the hospital to home or an agreed care destination.
detail: Coordinate your request with the discharge team. Share the expected ready time, destination, mobility needs and contact person; discharge readiness and ride availability must be confirmed.
question: Can a family member arrange a discharge ride?
answer: A family member or facility coordinator can request transportation and provide the pickup, destination and assistance details for review.
who: For a patient being released from a hospital to home or another agreed destination, with the transport type reviewed by the care team.
overview: Discharge transport depends on when the patient is actually ready to leave. Coordinate the pickup entrance, ready time, mobility needs and receiving contact with the discharge planner or nurse. If travel needs change, tell both teams before the ride; transportation does not replace discharge instructions or clinical care.
includes: Coordination with the discharge contact
Confirmed pickup and receiving destination
Mobility and handoff planning
prepare: Hospital entrance and discharge-team contact
Expected ready time, confirmed when released
Receiving person or facility and access details

faqs.q: Can you pick up before the discharge is complete?
faqs.a: The hospital must confirm the patient is ready for the agreed transport. Share the estimated time early, then update the transportation team when discharge timing is confirmed.

faqs.q: What if the patient cannot sit upright?
faqs.a: Ask the discharge team which transport type is appropriate. Stretcher transport and clinical monitoring are not among Compassion Care’s confirmed services; do not assume a standard ride will meet those needs.

title: Doctor appointments
heading: Make room for your health.
summary: Non-emergency rides to scheduled medical visits and outpatient appointments.
detail: Provide the time you need to arrive, not just the appointment start time. Discuss return transportation and any companion or mobility needs when requesting your trip.
question: What time should I request pickup?
answer: Share your required arrival time and both addresses. The team can review travel time and boarding needs before confirming pickup.
who: For a scheduled, non-emergency medical or outpatient visit when a passenger needs transportation assistance.
overview: A successful appointment trip starts with the clinic’s required arrival time, which may be earlier than the appointment itself. Provide the correct building and entrance, boarding needs and whether someone will accompany the passenger. Discuss the return separately, especially when the length of the appointment is uncertain.
includes: Planning around the required arrival time
Review of clinic access and mobility needs
One-way or requested return coordination
prepare: Clinic name, address and entrance
Required check-in time
Return estimate and companion request

faqs.q: Will the driver wait during my appointment?
faqs.a: Ask when requesting the trip. A scheduled return, a call-when-ready pickup and a driver waiting on site are different arrangements; waiting availability and charges require team confirmation.

faqs.q: Can I use this after sedation?
faqs.a: Ask the clinic what escort and discharge arrangements it requires. Transportation alone may not meet its responsible-adult policy; the clinic and transportation team must confirm the plan.

title: Dialysis transportation
heading: Support for the routine that matters.
summary: Transportation requests for dialysis visits, including recurring appointment schedules.
detail: Share treatment days, arrival times and expected return arrangements. Each recurring schedule needs team confirmation; changes in appointment times or assistance needs should be communicated.
question: Can I request recurring dialysis rides?
answer: Yes. Provide your appointment pattern and transportation requirements so the team can review a recurring schedule and confirm availability.
who: For trips to dialysis appointments, including requests for a repeated schedule.
overview: Dialysis transportation planning centers on a dependable appointment pattern and clear return arrangements. Share treatment days, required arrival and the center’s expected finish time. Tell the team about mobility or assistance needs for both legs, and report schedule changes promptly. Recurring rides still require confirmation of availability.
includes: Review of repeated appointment dates
Coordination of outward and return journeys
Updates when timing or mobility needs change
prepare: Treatment days and required arrival times
Dialysis-center contact and entrance
Expected finish time and return contact

faqs.q: Can the same weekly schedule be requested?
faqs.a: Yes. Share the full appointment pattern and assistance needs. The team must review the dates and confirm transportation; a recurring request does not reserve an unconfirmed vehicle.
Notify the transportation team as soon as the timing changes. Agree in advance who will call when the passenger is ready and how the return will be coordinated.

title: Rehabilitation appointments
heading: Keep moving toward your goals.
summary: Rides to physical therapy, rehabilitation and other scheduled recovery appointments.
detail: Let the team know about walking aids, boarding needs and changes in mobility. Transportation supports getting to appointments; therapy and treatment remain with your healthcare professionals.
question: Can transportation be arranged for repeated therapy visits?
answer: Provide the dates, required arrival times and mobility needs so the team can review your schedule and suitable transportation.
who: For travel to physical therapy, rehabilitation and other scheduled recovery appointments.
overview: Recovery needs can change between appointments. Tell the team what walking aids or wheelchair arrangements are needed now, rather than relying on a previous trip’s details. Include the therapy location, arrival time and return estimate. Transportation helps you reach treatment; exercise instructions and clinical decisions remain with the treating professionals.
includes: Planning around therapy appointments
Review of current mobility and access needs
Requests for repeated visits and returns
prepare: Therapy dates, location and arrival times
Current walking aid or wheelchair needs
Changes in boarding ability or assistance

faqs.q: Can I request transport for a course of therapy?
faqs.a: Yes. Provide the dates and expected appointment times so the team can review the full transportation request.

faqs.q: Does the driver provide rehabilitation treatment?
faqs.a: This is a transportation service. Therapy, transfers requiring clinical support and treatment instructions must be handled by the appropriate healthcare professionals.

title: Assisted living and nursing facility transportation
heading: Care continues between destinations.
summary: Coordinated transportation for assisted living and nursing facility residents.
detail: Facility staff or families can share resident transportation needs, pickup access, appointment details and the receiving contact. Confirm handoff responsibilities and return arrangements with the team.
question: Can a facility coordinate transportation for a resident?
answer: Yes. A facility coordinator can provide trip details and assistance needs for the transportation team to review.
who: For assisted living and nursing facility residents whose family or care team is coordinating a non-emergency trip.
overview: Facility transportation connects the resident, the sending facility and the receiving destination. Planning should identify who will have the resident ready, where the driver should meet them, and who will receive them after the trip. Confirm mobility needs, access arrangements and the return contact before transportation is accepted.
includes: Coordination with a family or facility contact
Resident mobility and pickup-access review
Sending and receiving handoff details
prepare: Facility name, entrance and coordinating contact
Resident’s current mobility and assistance needs
Receiving contact and return arrangements

faqs.q: Can facility staff request the ride?
faqs.a: Yes. A coordinator or family member can provide trip details. The team then reviews availability, assistance and handoff arrangements before confirming transportation.

faqs.q: Can a family member or caregiver come along?
faqs.a: Request companion space before booking. Seating, assistance responsibilities and any additional charges must be confirmed by the team.
